page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance within the Local SSDs family. It is built on KVM virtualization and driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache, alongside support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions.

Hardware provisioning combines 64.0 GB of system memory (providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio) with an integrated 1919 GB local SSD. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type. Network capabilities include a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps. The provision of substantial dedicated local NVMe/SSD capacity alongside a high memory footprint sets this instance apart from compute-centric configurations.

Synthetic benchmarks reflect the capabilities of an older-generation Xeon processor. General CPU execution yields lower-tier results, indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1101.68 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3584.0. PassMark overall CPU testing reaches 7005.33, falling within the mid-range bracket. Memory write performance remains balanced at 35.72 GB/sec for large un-cached blocks, and in-memory operations demonstrate stable throughput with 6.02 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given its combination of generous memory capacity, direct-attached local SSD storage, and modest CPU processing power, ecs.i2ne.2xlarge offers balanced hardware density without premium compute surcharges. It is particularly appropriate for memory-intensive caching layers, intermediate I/O-heavy data staging, NoSQL stores, and distributed database nodes that rely primarily on direct local storage and large memory allocations rather than raw single-threaded compute performance.

The server includes 64.0 GB of RAM and is bundled with a 1919 GB local SSD storage volume, supported by a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. No hardware GPU acceleration is included. Benchmark measurements reveal modest raw processor throughput, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 3584.0 and stress-ng multi-core scoring 5868.18, alongside stable memory write throughput of 35.72 GB/sec and 6.02 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance is best aligned with local-storage-dependent workloads, distributed databases, key-value stores, and caching engines requiring substantial memory-to-vCPU ratios alongside direct high-capacity local disk access.
